transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-21 15:00 PDT | Duration: 43m
Attendees: Tom (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood CSM), Maria Chen (CTO, Veridian), Jacob Li (Lead ML Eng), Nora Patel (Infra Lead), Samir Rao (Product)

00:00 Tom: hey everyone thanks for joining we can give a quick agenda, introduce priya who will walk through the quickstart and then dig into your constraints and timeline
00:09 Maria: thanks Tom, appreciate it. also just to be clear we have a 30 min window for tech and then we can do follow ups, hope that's OK
00:14 Tom: perfect, i'll keep it tight
00:18 Priya: hi all, quick one line intro — i'm priya, se on infra and perf for redwood. today i'll show the quickstart flow, what a free trial looks like, and typical time-to-first-token we see for hosted. then open to dedicated/private conversations
00:34 Jacob: great, we're mainly evaluating how fast we can get a demo out to product buyers. so time-to-first-token and easy sdk are key. also cost if we get high traffic from demos
00:45 Nora: and from infra side we need to know data retention and encryption/KMS options. we are regulated so SOC2 matters.
00:54 Tom: totally, that's pretty aligned with other customers. quick question on current stack — what are you using today for model infra?
01:02 Maria: mostly using a managed endpoint on c-p vendor and some on-prem experiments. we've used openai for quick prototyping but want less vendor lock and better unit economics for production
01:14 Jacob: we also run some retrained open models on k8s with custom serving. but setup overhead is high and latency inconsistent for short demos
01:27 Priya: understood. for quickstart hosted api — it's a couple steps: sign up, get credits, run the simple curl or sdk to call text generation, we have code examples for node/python and a one-file demo app. Typical time-to-first-token is 5-12 minutes for an engineer (account create -> sdk key -> first request), and first observable output stream in ~200-400ms for a small model. If you use our smallest curated model you'll see lower latency.
01:53 Samir: 5-12 minutes? that's very promising. does that include provisioning anything else?
01:58 Priya: yep that's pure developer path assuming hosted mode. No infra to provision. If you want dedicated i can explain the reserved capacity path — that'll take longer because of capacity sizing and contracts, usually weeks.
02:10 Nora: how do you handle keys and KMS? we need customer-managed keys ideally
02:15 Tom: good point. for hosted we offer Redwood-managed keys by default but there is a private deployment option where you can bring your KMS/HSM. We also have enterprise options for customer-managed keys in a dedicated control plane — i'll follow up with the SOC2 and security pack links.
02:29 Maria: is there an option for VPC peering for hosted? our security team asks for network isolation for some features
02:36 Priya: hosted is internet-based, but Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private supports full VPC/on-prem. For many customers we do dedicated for production so they can get the latency guarantees + VPC.
02:49 Jacob: curious on cost tradeoffs — for demos that spike traffic is hosted more expensive than dedicated?
02:55 Priya: generally hosted is simplest and good for prototyping; dedicated reduces per-token cost once you hit predictable throughput. We provide batching, quantization suggestions and an optimize toolkit to reduce costs. For bursty demo traffic, dedicated can be configured with burst pools to avoid capacity issues but it requires commit. There is also fallback routing to compatible model variants if primary is saturated.
03:20 Samir: ok that helps. do you have a sandbox or org-wide trial so product can try without buying?
03:26 Tom: yes we provision trial credits to the org plus developer keys per user — that's how most PLG flows start. We'll send an invite link and example curl.
03:34 Maria: what about rate limits? we need to demo 10 concurrent users hitting the endpoint
03:39 Priya: hosted plans have rate limits per account but can be raised for trials; for 10 concurrent it's fine on hosted, you might see slightly higher latency but still acceptable. We'll include guidance on batching to keep cost down and latency reasonable.
03:53 Jacob: any gotchas with streaming and function calling? we plan to use tool-calling for a retrieval plugin
03:59 Priya: streaming works out-of-box and function/tool calling is supported. small note: sometimes the naming in our docs had a leftover from older product names — if you see a mismatch let us know, docs occasionally have typos.
04:12 Nora: on compliance — can you share your SOC2 report and data residency options? we operate in eu and na
04:18 Tom: yes — we'll share SOC2 and regional deployment docs. Hosted has region-specific endpoints; Dedicated/private give more control.
04:27 Maria: what's the ramp to dedicated if the pilot goes well? timeline and cost?
04:31 Priya: typically after a successful pilot you engage our sales/solutions team. Dedicated onboarding including capacity sizing, autoscale configuration, and SLA setup is commonly 4-8 weeks depending on size. Cost is commit-based — we'll provide a model.
04:47 Samir: in pilot what metrics should we measure to decide success?
04:52 Priya: good question — we recommend throughput (requests/min), p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy/regression on a sample evaluation set. Also error rates and fallback frequency if you have routing policies.
05:06 Maria: ok. we have a privacy question — for hosted, do you log prompts? can customers opt-out?
05:12 Tom: by default, we retain minimal logs for billing/observability but enterprise plans have options for log retention and disabling training/usage. We'll share the data retention controls in the security pack.
05:24 Jacob: one more technical — what's the expected latency for a 1k token generation on a small-medium model on hosted?
05:31 Priya: depends on model and seq length. For smaller curated models we often see ~300-700ms per chunk for shorter responses; large gen of 1k tokens will be higher — a few seconds — and that's where batching/kv cache and kernel selection matter. Dedicated with right GPU and quantization can reduce that.
05:52 Maria: can you do a live demo of the quickstart now? we have 15 minutes left
05:56 Tom: sure priya, do you want to share your screen
06:00 Priya: i'm going to paste the quickstart repo link — i won't paste the entire code here but will run through it. step 1, sign up and create api key. step 2, install sdk or curl call: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-small-1","input":"hello"}'`. That returns streamed events.
06:26 Nora: sometimes our security team blocks curl to external endpoints, can we test via a local proxy or a restricted network?
06:33 Priya: yeah you can route through a proxy; we also have an sdk that supports custom transport. We'll include example with proxies in the quickstart.
06:43 Priya: demo: I created a quick key earlier for this call, i'm going to run the example. first request... (typing sounds)
06:57 Priya: you can see response streaming back, this is on hosted, latency was about 320ms for the first chunk.
07:05 Jacob: the stream looked clean. what's the token pricing and how do i estimate cost for QA?
07:11 Tom: pricing is per-token for hosted; we'll share sample cost calculators. For pilots we often pre-load sample traffic to estimate. Also use Redwood Optimize to propose batching/quantization for cost reduction.
07:25 Maria: what if we need SSO for developer accounts?
07:28 Tom: we support SAML/SSO for enterprise orgs and role-based access control. For quick trials we provide invite links but SSO can be turned on in the org settings for production.
07:40 Samir: are there any restrictions on model weights/llama licensing et cetera?
07:44 Priya: our catalog includes curated open models and proprietary variants; licensing is handled per model. If you want to bring-your-own model in Private or Dedicated we have a model onboarding process.
07:56 Maria: timeline — we want a working demo for execs in two weeks. realistic?
08:01 Priya: yes for a hosted quickstart with our SDK and sample dataset two weeks is realistic. If you need dedicated it will push beyond that.
08:10 Tom: recap before we close — we'll send quickstart snippets, trial credits, SOC2/security pack, and schedule a dedicated perf demo next week. Anything else?
08:19 Maria: please include the sample curl and node snippet. also include any example latency numbers for redwood-small-1 vs redwood-medium-1.
08:27 Priya: will do, i'll attach a perf checklist.
08:30 Nora: request: can priya also include steps to set up org-level SSO and customer-managed KMS options?
08:35 Tom: noted, we'll include both.
08:38 Maria: thanks everyone, this was super helpful. we'll aim to try the quickstart tomorrow and update you on blockers.
08:45 Tom: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with links and credits.

(occasional crosstalk and filler, timestamps approximate and transcription imperfect, some product names abbreviated or slightly mis-transcribed)

End of transcript.
